definitions.explanation: A hollow ceramic pig with an opening in its side, used to hold a burning mosquito coil. A familiar emblem of Japanese summer, often seen on verandas and in seasonal advertising.

examples.japanese: {縁側|えんがわ}に{蚊遣|かや}り{豚|ぶた}が{置|お}いてある。
examples.english: A mosquito coil pig is sitting on the veranda.

examples.japanese: {蚊遣|かや}り{豚|ぶた}は{夏|なつ}の{風物詩|ふうぶつし}だ。
examples.english: The mosquito coil pig is one of the sights of summer.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{家|いえ}では、{今|いま}でも{蚊遣|かや}り{豚|ぶた}に{蚊取|かと}り{線香|せんこう}を{入|い}れて{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: At my grandmother's house they still put mosquito coils in the ceramic pig and use it.

notes:
From {蚊遣|かや}り (driving off mosquitoes) plus {豚|ぶた} (pig). Also written {蚊取|かと}り{豚|ぶた}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蚊遣|かや}り{豚|ぶた}を{置|お}く: to set out a mosquito coil pig
- {夏|なつ}の{風物詩|ふうぶつし}: a seasonal sight of summer
- {蚊取|かと}り{線香|せんこう}を{入|い}れる: to put a coil inside it

CULTURAL NOTE:
The shape is said to derive from Edo-period pots used to burn smoky material against mosquitoes. Today it is as much a nostalgic ornament as a practical device, and it appears constantly in summer illustrations alongside wind chimes and watermelon.
